=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:482-486 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The MCP branch accepts any mcp__*__issue_write call whose labels list contains ai:claude-blocked, without inspecting the tool_input["method"] field.
  WHY: An unattended session can post a real blocked comment, then call mcp__*__issue_write with method: "delete", labels: ["ai:claude-blocked"], and issue_number set to the marker's issue. The hook records the call as a verified label write on the marker issue (the target resolves via _mcp_issue_target, and BLOCKED_LABEL is in the labels list), the tool actually removes the existing blocker label, and the session can end its turn on a question after silently stripping the very label the hook requires. The test helper _mcp_label always sets method: "update", so this path has zero test coverage for non-update methods.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:265-272 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: _contains_marker is defined but has zero callers after the rewrite of blocked_comment_posted.
  WHY: No runtime failure from dead code alone, but the function name and body still describe exactly the old, weaker "marker-anywhere" check that issue #5082 fixed. In a security hook, dead code that mirrors a check the issue says was the attack surface invites a future maintainer to believe that check is still active and to "strengthen" the new path by re-introducing the call, which would silently re-open the bypass this PR exists to close.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  WHY: If mcp__*__issue_write ever supports a method other than "update" that takes a labels list and removes labels (or creates a new issue with those labels while ignoring issue_number), the hook would count it as a verified label write on the marker issue.   PROBLEM: The MCP branch of _blocked_label_targets accepts any mcp__*__issue_write call whose labels list contains ai:claude-blocked without inspecting the method field.
  WHY: A session could call it with method: "create", issue_number matching the marker, and labels: ["ai:claude-blocked"]. The create method creates a new issue with those labels while ignoring issue_number, but the hook counts it as a verified label write on the marker's issue because it only checks that issue_number matches. The label result is not URL-verified (only the comment result is), so the bypass is silent. This is exactly the spoofing class this PR exists to close (STRIDE: Spoofing, issue #5082).
